newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-CRONJE SPURS SOUTH AFRICA TO VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-CRONJE SPURS SOUTH AFRICA TO VICTORY.

text.p: Captain Hansie Cronje underlined his prolific form in the triangular series by hammering an unbeaten 70 from 86 balls to fire South Africa to a four-wicket victory over Zimbabwe at the Wanderers on Friday.
Cronje came in with South Africa in trouble at 72 for four in pursuit of Zimbabwe's 50-over total of 256 for eight, and he took them to success at 259 for six from 48.3 overs in the day-night game.

The South African skipper, whose fifth four was the winning boundary, blasted 87 not out against Zimbabwe at Centurion Park a week ago. He has been dismissed only once in the tournament, which also features India, and is averaging 223.
All-rounder Shaun Pollock shared a brilliant sixth wicket stand of 137 with Cronje as the pair rebuilt the innings from the depths of 102 for five in the 20th over.

Pollock made 75, his highest one-day international score, from 85 balls with five fours and helped beat the sixth wicket record for South Africa of 88 by Dave Richardson and Jonty Rhodes, made against Pakistan two years ago.
Zimbabwe opening bowler Eddo Brandes ripped out the first three wickets in his opening spell to reduce the home side to 16 for three.
Rhodes (34) and Daryll Cullinan (30) began the recovery, but it was not until Cronje and Pollock lifted the tempo towards the end of the innings that South Africa looked likely winners.
Zimbabwe built their total around half-centuries from Grant Flower and Dave Houghton and inspired lower order hitting from Guy Whittall and Paul Strang.
Flower made 62 at the top of the order and put on 93 for the fifth wicket with Houghton, who made a sparkling 57 from 61 balls, hitting four fours and a six.

When Flower fell with the score at 168 for six, Whittall (41) and Strang (40 not out) smashed 63 in 10 overs to ensure a healthy score. But on a perfect batting pitch they were still a little short of a defendable total as Cronje and Pollock later proved.
South Africa, who now have four wins from as many matches, play India at Port Elizabeth on Sunday in the next series match.
